
[[File:Kanseikaku.jpg|thumb|240x240px|An example of a jungle bath<small>{{ill|Harazuru Onsen Kanseikaku|de|Harazuru Onsen Kanseikaku|ja|原鶴温泉咸生閣|zh|原鹤温泉咸生阁|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579539}} (2004-08-28)</small>]]
'''Janguruburo''' (ジャングル風呂) is a large-scale bathing facility in which various types of tubs—such as {{ill|large communal bath|de|große Gemeinschaftsbäder|ja|大浴場|zh|大型公共浴池}} and {{ill|family bath|de|Familienbad|ja|家族風呂|zh|家庭浴池}}—are installed inside a greenhouse lush with tropical plants. Users are, in principle, required to be naked, just as in a standard {{ill|Public bathing|af|Baddens in Klassieke Tyd|ar|حمامات عامة|az|İctimai hamam|ca|Banys públics|cdo|Tŏng-diè-dáing|de|Badehaus|eo|Banejo|es|Baños públicos (historia)|eu|Bainuetxe publiko|fa|حمام عمومی|fi|Yleinen sauna|fr|Bains publics|he|בית מרחץ|id|Pemandian umum|is|Baðhús|ja|公衆浴場|jv|Jedhing umum|ko|목욕탕|lt|Garinė pirtis|nl|Badhuis|nn|Badehus|pt|Banho público|simple|Bathhouse|sv|Badhus|tr|Hamam|vi|Nhà tắm công cộng|zh|公眾浴場|zh_yue|浴堂|qid=Q785952|lt=Public Bathhouse}}. In some facilities, {{ill|Onsen|ar|أونسن|az|Onsen|bcl|Onsen|ca|Onsen|cs|Onsen|da|Onsen|de|Onsen|el|Όνσεν|eo|Onsen|es|Onsen|et|Onsen|eu|Onsen|fa|اونسن|fi|Onsen|fr|Onsen|he|אונסן|hu|Onszen|id|Onsen|it|Onsen|ja|温泉|km|អុនសេន|ko|일본의 온천|la|Onsen|lt|Onsenas|lv|Onsens|ms|Onsen|my|အွန်းဆန်း|nl|Onsen|nn|Onsen|no|Onsen|pl|Onsen|pt|Onsen|ro|Onsen|ru|Онсэн|simple|Onsen|sk|Onsen|sl|Onsen|sv|Onsen|ta|ஒன்சென்|th|อนเซ็ง|tl|Onsen|tr|Onsen|uk|Онсен|ur|اونسن|vi|Onsen|zh|日本溫泉|qid=Q655311|lt=hot spring water}} is {{ill|Drawn‐off hot spring|ja|引湯|qid=Q11487160|lt=Drawn‐off}} from nearby springs.

== Overview ==
A type of large-scale bathing facility often installed in {{ill|health land|ja|健康ランド|qid=Q11387182}} or large-scale {{ill|onsen ryokan|ja|温泉宿|qid=Q11562938}}. These are typically built in daylight-lit buildings of at least 150 tsubo (roughly 495 m²). Within the bathing area, artificial hills and tropical gardens are installed, or a shallow, circulating {{ill|Bathtub|an|Banyera|ar|مغطس|arz|بانيو|ast|Bañera|az|Vanna|ba|Ванна|bar|Bodwann|be|Ванна|bg|Вана|br|Kibell|ca|Banyera|ckb|بانیۆ|cs|Vana|da|Badekar|de|Badewanne|el|Μπανιέρα|eo|Banujo|es|Bañera|et|Vann|eu|Bainuontzi|fa|وان (حمام)|fi|Kylpyamme|fr|Baignoire|ga|Folcadán|gd|Ballan|gl|Bañeira|he|אמבטיה|hi|स्नानपात्र|hr|Kada|hy|Լոգարան|id|Bak mandi|ig|Ebe ịsa ahụ|is|Baðker|it|Vasca da bagno|ja|浴槽|jv|Jedhing|ka|აბაზანა|kk|Ванна|ko|욕조|ksh|Büdd|ky|Ванна|la|Labrum|lb|Buedbidden|lt|Vonia|lv|Vanna|nds_nl|Badkupe|nl|Badkuip|nn|Badekar|no|Badekar|pl|Wanna|pt|Banheira|qu|Ch'illami|ro|Cadă|ru|Ванна|sd|غسل ٽپ|simple|Bath|sk|Vaňa|sl|Kopalna kad|sr|Када|sv|Badkar|ta|குளியல் தொட்டி|tr|Küvet|tyv|Ванна|uk|Ванна|uz|Vanna|vi|Bồn tắm|wuu|浴缸|yi|וואנע|zh|浴缸|zh_min_nan|E̍k-tháng|zh_yue|沖涼缸|qid=Q152095|lt=bath pool}} runs around the entire space to simulate a tropical {{ill|Tropical rainforest|en|Tropical rainforest|qid=Q199403|lt=jungle rainforest}}. Facilities often include artificial {{ill|Waterfall|en|Waterfall|qid=Q34038|lt=waterfalls}} or exploration-style {{ill|Cave|en|Cave|qid=Q35509|lt=caves}} to add entertainment value for children, though many advertise {{ill|Mixed bathing|en|Mixed bathing|qid=Q6883947|lt=mixed bathing}} as a draw<ref name="the sun">『太陽』1976年1月号 NO.152「九州へんな温泉旅」藤原審爾</ref>.

A common feature is a water spout modeled after the face of a {{ill|Lion|en|Lion|qid=Q140|lt=lion}} or a {{ill|Tiger|en|Tiger|qid=Q19939|lt=tiger}}. Until relatively recently, many communal taps were imported from Britain; in Europe since the Middle Ages, the lion has been regarded as the guardian deity of water (in contrast to Japan and China, where the dragon serves that role, giving rise to the term "蛇口" ["faucet"]).

In terms of enjoying scenery and atmosphere, these share elements with {{ill|outdoor baths|de|Freiluftbad|ja|露天風呂|zh|露天浴池}} and indoor {{ill|rock baths|de|Felsenbad|ja|岩風呂|zh|岩浴池|qid=Q113498032}}. However, because they require labor-intensive care for living plants, they have gradually disappeared. Some onsen hotels, however, actively promote and utilize them as entertainment facilities.

Their heyday was during the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa era}}, making them objects of retro or Shōwa nostalgia. From around 1965 to 1975, many health centers featured jungle baths.

The author {{ill|Shinji Fujiwara|de|Shinji Fujiwara|ja|藤原審爾|zh|藤原審爾|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11623205}}, who had extensive {{ill|Thermal bath|de|Heilbad|ja|湯治|zh|温泉疗养|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1004887}} experience in his youth due to {{ill|Tuberculosis|de|Lungentuberkulose|ja|肺結核|zh|肺结核|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 結核|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q12204}}, contributed an account of his stay at the jungle bath of the Ibusuki Kankō Hotel to the January 1976 issue of the magazine 『太陽』. Although he had thought {{ill|Ibusuki|en|Ibusuki|qid=Q19712|lt=Ibusuki}} to be as remote and obscure as {{ill|Sukumo, Kōchi|en|Sukumo, Kōchi|qid=Q655258|lt=Sukumo}} on Shikoku, the large tourist hotel was noisy as if he had stayed at a station, offering nothing like tranquility. He noted that the jungle bath had about thirty separate baths, and its main attraction was the mixed bathing: a lively group of young women made it worth a look, although the women's-only bath was occupied by men, so that roughly 80% of users were men and children, 10% were older women, and the remaining 10% were mothers with children<ref name="the sun"/>.

== Origin ==
The jungle bath is said to have originated at {{ill|Ibusuki Onsen|en|Ibusuki Onsen|qid=Q5984938|lt=Ibusuki Hot Springs}}. The first jungle bath, installed at the Ibusuki Kankō Hotel, was recognized as a local specialty of Ibusuki<ref>{{Cite book ja-jp| author = 武田幸一 |year = 1973| title = カラーブックス23『九州の旅』| publisher = 保育社| pages = 90}}</ref>. Another theory credits the villa of ornithologist {{ill|Masauji Hachisuka|en|Masauji Hachisuka|qid=Q11625684|lt=Masashi Hachisuka}} in {{ill|Atami|en|Atami|qid=Q653364|lt=Atami}} (built 1933, demolished 1986), where a large bath was planted with tropical flora, as the true origin<ref>{{Cite book ja-jp| author = [[藤森照信]],[[荒俣宏]]| title =『東京路上博物誌』| publisher = [[鹿島出版会]] | year=1987| isbn = 4-306-09303-4}}</ref>.
